answer: In an agent economy each interaction vertex can open a fresh work thread only after binding a unique relic of its prior signed attestations. Forging an extra fake identity forces the attacker to mint and extend a separate relic chain, paying linear compute plus storage that grows with every new thread length, whereas one honest agent reuses a single accumulating relic. The marginal cost per additional sybil therefore rises with both the number of heads and the depth of each forged thread.
